name: Early Lake Turkana pastoralism
description: Communities near Lake Turkana combined herding domestic animals with fishing during the early Pastoral Neolithic.

impact.note: The arrival of herding in eastern Africa gave regional communities a new livelihood that later pastoral societies there continued.

date.label: Approximately 5000 years BP (3050 BCE)
date.basis: Source-reported period or approximate chronology; where calibrated BP is stated, converted using the 1950 reference epoch.

events.statement: Communities near Lake Turkana combined herding domestic animals with fishing during the early Pastoral Neolithic.
events.caveats: The date is a broad regional approximation rather than a dated first adoption event; genetic, archaeological and cultural pathways of herding transmission are incompletely resolved.

evidence.supports: The review of archaeological evidence describes herding and fishing near Lake Turkana at the beginning of the Pastoral Neolithic around 5000 BP.

date.label: Dongodien context, c. 5000–4500 cal BP
date.basis: Grillo et al. Table 1 gives the site range. The calendar years use the dataset’s 1950 BP conversion.

events.statement: One residue from a ceramic vessel at the Dongodien herder-fisher settlement falls in the ruminant dairy range.
events.place_note: Dongodien (GaJi4) on the eastern shore of Lake Turkana.
events.caveats: This is one of five interpretable residues at the site. The range applies to the site context. Herd species, degree of dietary reliance, and exact dairy preparation remain unresolved.

evidence.locator: Table 1; Lipid residue results, Meat and milk; Fig. 4
evidence.supports: Dongodien yielded a pottery residue in the ruminant dairy range, alongside evidence for other animal and possible plant products.

earliest_record.rationale: Earliest source-supported dated event for this scoped record; not a global priority claim. The date is a broad regional approximation rather than a dated first adoption event; genetic, archaeological and cultural pathways of herding transmission are incompletely resolved.

unresolved.note: Neither local dairy residues nor the human ancestry data identify a transfer from Takarkori or any other named upstream settlement.
